## Research findings

The premise that Yudkowsky is only a writer and "not a scientist of any kind" is factually false. He is also described as a decision theorist whose work is cited in Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig's textbook Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky). He has authored peer-reviewed / academic publications including chapters in Global Catastrophic Risks (Oxford University Press), Singularity Hypotheses (Springer), The Cambridge Handbook of Artificial Intelligence, and papers in AGI 2011 and AAAI Workshops (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky). The writer part is true — he wrote Rationality: From AI to Zombies, LessWrong/Overcoming Bias posts, Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality, and If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky) — but "not a scientist of any kind" directly contradicts his researcher/fellow status and scientific publication record. Lack of formal credentials — "autodidact" who "did not attend high school or college" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky) — does not equal not being a scientist/researcher of any kind.
